body: Hi, is it possible to get this PR reviewed before v4.7?
Unfortunately the Godot network team is in a low activity state and thus we are having trouble keeping up with network PRs. I'll ask in chat if someone else is available to review it.

> This change results in the thread stalling potentially indefinitely in that loop.

Hi @Faless, thanks for the review (and thank @Ivorforce for bringing this PR up in chat). In case of the thread potentially stalling in `StreamPeerTCP::wait`, the PR has updated to 3474daa395e467a094408a53b34d3582f5a44939 with the following change:

1. Added `HTTPClient::disconnect_from_host` method that will close the connection socket without deleting it (only `HTTPClientTCP` has actual implementation at the moment).
2. In `HTTPRequest::cancel_request`, if blocking mode is set, `HTTPClient::disconnect_from_host` is called first to close the connection before waiting for the thread to finish (once the socket is closed, `StreamPeerTCP::wait` calls should return immediately).

6ef8612b506e159ccba1ab9d19995afe406e7550 replaces `_THREAD_SAFE_*` macros with another approach by setting client status ahead of `tcp_connection->disconnect_from_host()` in `HTTPClientTCP::disconnect_from_host`.

Apologies for constantly pushing the change.

<!-- Draft review comment for https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/117749 — NOT posted.
     Alternative branch, not pushed: ~/Developer/godot-pr-http-stall (fix-http-threaded-stall,
     commit "HTTPClientTCP: Don't spin forever on a silent peer in blocking mode"). -->

Tested this PR on 4.7.2-stable (macOS arm64, cherry-picked onto ed1daf0bf) against a server that accepts the connection and never sends a byte. It fixes the common case, but there is still a race that can freeze the main thread.

**Repro.** The server accepts and holds every connection:

```python
import socket
s = socket.socket(); s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 18765)); s.listen(8)
held = []
while True:
    c, _ = s.accept(); held.append(c)
```

The script makes three threaded `HTTPRequest`s, each stalled for 2 s, then ends one with `cancel_request()`, one with `remove_child()` (`EXIT_TREE`), and one with `timeout = 4.0`, timing the main thread:

```gdscript
extends SceneTree

func _init() -> void:
	_run.call_deferred()

func _run() -> void:
	for how in ["cancel", "free", "timeout"]:
		var http := HTTPRequest.new()
		http.use_threads = true
		if how == "timeout":
			http.timeout = 4.0
		root.add_child(http)
		http.request("http://127.0.0.1:18765/x")
		await create_timer(2.0).timeout
		var t := Time.get_ticks_msec()
		match how:
			"cancel":
				http.cancel_request()
				print("cancel_request: %d ms" % (Time.get_ticks_msec() - t))
				http.queue_free()
			"free":
				root.remove_child(http)
				print("EXIT_TREE: %d ms" % (Time.get_ticks_msec() - t))
				http.free()
			"timeout":
				await http.request_completed
				print("timeout fired after %d ms" % (Time.get_ticks_msec() - t))
				http.queue_free()
	quit()
```

`godot --headless --script stall.gd`

**Results with this exact script, 4.7.2 + each patch, one batch each:**

| build | runs that froze | main thread blocked when it didn't |
|---|---|---|
| stock | 2 of 2 (on the first `cancel_request()`) | — |
| this PR | 2 of 12 (both in `EXIT_TREE`); a longer variant of the script froze in the `timeout` case too | 0–1 ms |
| bounded wait (below) | 0 of 10 | 6–48 ms |

**Backtrace of a freeze with this PR** (`timeout` case, debug symbols):

```
thread #1 (main)
  __ulock_wait
  _pthread_join
  Thread::wait_to_finish()          thread_apple.cpp:137
  HTTPRequest::cancel_request()
  HTTPRequest::_timeout()
  ...
thread #14
  poll
  NetSocketUnix::poll(NetSocket::PollType, int) const
  HTTPClientTCP::_get_http_data(unsigned char*, int, int&)
  HTTPClientTCP::poll()
  HTTPRequest::_update_connection()
  HTTPRequest::_thread_func(void*)
```

So `disconnect_from_host()` was called but did not wake the `wait(POLL_TYPE_IN, -1)`. My reading (from the code, not confirmed in a debugger): `NetSocketUnix::poll` checks `is_open()` and then copies `_sock` into `pfd.fd`. If the main thread's `close()` lands between the two, `_sock` is already `-1`, and `::poll()` ignores a negative fd, so with timeout `-1` it sleeps forever. Closing the socket from another thread also leaves `_sock` as an unsynchronized read/write between the two threads.

A simpler alternative, that avoids touching the socket from another thread: never wait without a bound. When nothing has arrived, wait at most 50 ms and return the short read. Every caller of `_get_http_data` already handles a short read, because that is the non-blocking contract. The thread loop then regains control and sees `thread_request_quit`:

```cpp
		while (left > 0) {
			err = connection->get_partial_data(p_buffer + r_received, left, read);
			if (err == OK && read == 0) {
				if (tcp_connection.is_valid() && tcp_connection->get_status() == StreamPeerTCP::STATUS_CONNECTED) {
					tcp_connection->wait(NetSocket::POLL_TYPE_IN, 50);
				}
				return OK;
			}
			...
```

This removes the busy-wait as well (the thread sleeps in `poll()`). It does not cover two things this PR targets: a stall inside a blocking `put_data` (a peer that stops reading a large upload), and a stall during DNS resolution. Cancel latency is bounded by the poll interval, so it is up to 50 ms rather than ~0.

Also checked with the bounded wait: HTTPS (two real hosts, byte-identical bodies, same timings), chunked and large bodies, slow and dropped connections, HTML 5xx bodies and 429 retries, through a stub server, with results identical to stock.

I can open this as a separate PR if that is preferred, or happy to see it folded into this one.
